bullets.title: BOJ hikes to 1.25%, signals further tightening; yen weakens
bullets.body: The Bank of Japan raised its overnight call rate 25bp to 1.25% as widely expected—its highest level since 1995—with Governor Ueda noting no policy options excluded, including larger or repeated hikes. Ueda cautioned that overly rapid tightening risks overshooting and flagged yen weakness as a potential upside inflation risk; USD/JPY rose ~1% to ~156.80 post-announcement. Citi now forecasts additional 25bp BOJ hikes in Dec 2026, Mar 2027, and Jul 2027.

bullets.title: Goldman sees Fed hiking in October; Polymarket at 62% probability
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs revised its Fed outlook to expect a rate hike in October, one week before the midterm elections. Polymarket odds of another hike this year sit at 62%. US headline CPI held at 3.4% YoY and core at 2.4% in August, both above the 2% target.

bullets.title: Germany PPI jumps to 4.6% YoY in August, well above 3.9% estimate
bullets.body: Germany's August PPI came in at 4.6% YoY versus a 3.9% consensus estimate and 3.0% prior, with MoM at 1.1% versus 0.6% expected. The print reinforces persistent upstream inflation pressure in Europe.

bullets.title: UK retail sales beat strongly in August, consumer resilience intact
bullets.body: UK August retail sales (inc. auto fuel) rose 2.4% YoY vs. 1.9% estimate and 1.6% prior, while ex-auto fuel came in at 2.7% vs. 1.9% estimate. MoM beat of +0.5% vs. -0.2% consensus reverses July's -0.5%.

bullets.title: India buys record $15.2B in US Treasuries in July; China holdings at post-GFC lows
bullets.body: India's July Treasury purchases of $15.2B represent the largest monthly buy on record, signaling strong foreign central bank demand for dollar assets. Separately, China's US Treasury holdings fell to their lowest level since the 2008 global financial crisis.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz vessel traffic drops sharply; tanker struck; WTI near $96.50
bullets.body: Commodity vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz fell to just 4 vessels on Thursday versus a 10-day average of ~16, with Iran's IRGC claiming a strike on the Togo-flagged tanker Trend. WTI crude is consolidating below $96.50, and diesel hit an all-time high of $6.40/gallon while US gas prices reached $4.43/gallon—the highest level ever for this point in September.

bullets.title: NVDA CEO: expects chip sales to double next year; short-side skeptic eyes TomorrowXSummit
bullets.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang projected NVDA will sell twice as many chips next year versus the current year. One fintwit analyst maintaining a short thesis on NVDA nonetheless flagged Jensen's upcoming TomorrowXSummit appearance as 75% messaging catalyst versus 25% corporate action for a potential narrative shift.

bullets.title: INTC CEO flags 5-7x memory price surge; shortage worsening in 2027
bullets.body: Intel CEO reportedly stated at the AI Infra Summit 2026 in Santa Clara that memory prices have risen 5-7x and the shortage is expected to worsen in 2027—seen as bullish read-through for SNDK and MU. Separately, the prior session saw INTC +9.8% on a report of a potential US memory chip manufacturing deal with SK Hynix, while MRVL gained +5.4%.

bullets.title: MRVL expands GlobalFoundries deal for AI optical networking; TSEM begins 800G/1.6T shipments
bullets.body: Marvell and GlobalFoundries expanded their multi-year chip-capacity agreement for AI data-center optical connectivity. Separately, Tower Semiconductor (TSEM) and NewPhotonics commenced high-volume shipments of laser-integrated silicon photonics optical engines on its PH18DA SiPho platform supporting 800G and 1.6T standards; TSEM gained +8.43% in the prior session.

bullets.title: CPO/silicon photonics testing bottleneck remains; VIAV flagged at Computex
bullets.body: A six-month follow-up analysis on the silicon photonics and CPO testing bottleneck finds testing capacity still gating deployments, with NVIDIA's Spectrum-X Ethernet initiative now moving from roadmap to production phase. VIAV was noted at Computex 2026 for its module and final testing role; LITE also flagged as an optical test beneficiary.

bullets.title: AMD raising chip prices ~10% in Q4 on TSMC cost pass-through
bullets.body: Per ChannelGate reporting cited on fintwit, AMD plans to increase chip prices approximately 10% in Q4 as TSMC's own price increases flow through to production costs.

bullets.title: TSMC plans 3 sub-1.4nm fabs in Taiwan; $31B+ investment, first mass production by 2030
bullets.body: TSMC plans to build three new fabs for sub-1.4nm chip manufacturing in Longtan, north Taiwan, with the first targeted for mass production by 2030 and total investment exceeding NT$1 trillion (~US$31.4B).

bullets.title: SK Hynix launches Silicon Valley venture arm; Solidigm pursuing first US NAND fab
bullets.body: SK Hynix established 'SK Hynix Ventures' in Silicon Valley focused on global AI ecosystem investments. Separately, its subsidiary Solidigm is pursuing plans to build its first US NAND flash fab. Chinese rival CXMT is also reportedly planning a NAND flash research line in Beijing.

bullets.title: Japan-US in talks for $19.3B GlobalFoundries chip fab as part of Japan's $550B US investment pledge
bullets.body: Japan and the US are discussing a ¥2–3 trillion (~$19.3B) chip fab to be built and operated by GlobalFoundries in the US, tied to Japan's broader $550B tariff-related US investment commitment.

bullets.title: Waymo plans Singapore commercial robotaxi launch by 2028
bullets.body: Alphabet-owned Waymo announced vehicles arriving in Singapore later this year for a mapping and learning phase starting early 2027, with a full commercial robotaxi service planned for 2028.

bullets.title: META's Muse AI claimed to rank #1 globally, beating ChatGPT; AR hardware advancing
bullets.body: A fintwit post claimed META's Muse AI model hit the top global ranking, surpassing ChatGPT. Separately, one observer noted Meta's AR glasses are smaller and cheaper than competitors but less advanced, with the AR category expected to see major growth within 18 months.

bullets.title: PLTR CEO Karp: token discounts are about accessing customer IP, not market share
bullets.body: Palantir CEO Alex Karp told CNBC that token discounts are used to gain access to customer IP to improve Palantir's models, not primarily for market expansion. Separately, Palantir is building a Foundry-hosted food safety risk platform for Chipotle that aggregates health inspections, pest incidents, and employee illness data.

bullets.title: Goldman forecasts $420B hyperscaler gross debt issuance in 2027, up 68% on higher CapEx
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs now expects $420B of hyperscaler gross debt issuance in 2027, up ~68% from a $250B 2026 estimate, driven by upward CapEx revisions. That would equal roughly half of new Treasury long-duration borrowing in 2027.

bullets.title: AI agents already majority of inference; token consumption to accelerate
bullets.body: One fintwit account noted that AI agents already represent the majority of inference today and that 'within 1-2 years, nearly all inference will be agent-driven,' with most tokens consumed by agents executing background tasks 24/7—a bullish signal for AI infrastructure demand.

bullets.title: Phison CEO: single customer ordered 800PB of SSD storage in May; demand now normalizing
bullets.body: Phison's CEO K.S. Pua revealed that a single customer ordered 800 petabytes of SSD storage in May but that customer demand has since normalized after the initial rush—suggesting a possible air pocket in enterprise SSD demand.
